brief: Pull B is tonight, 24 November, the last day of the build block; the lighter week starts tomorrow. Push B on 23 November was your first night since 17 November and it went well: shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four sets, chest press 165 for 10 on all three, reverse pec deck 97.5 for 13 on all three, crossover 30.5 for 15, 15. You did three of the four lateral raise sets and wrote asking why four; the answer is under your notes below, and the short version is that side delts are what widens your shoulders on stage, four sets is the bottom of the research range and not the top, and I would rather you did them than that I cut them. The program is now version 16. The only changes are two rep ranges, from 8 to 10 up to 8 to 12 on the dumbbell shoulder press and the chest-supported row. Both cards told you four 10s earn the next dumbbell (55 and 65) and your rack has neither, it goes 50, 60, 70; I was wrong to say so, and now the reps climb to 12 before the jump. Tonight's Pull B: chest-supported row 60 for 10 on all four. Close-grip pulldown 120 for 10, then 135 for 9, 9. Straight-arm pulldown 52.5 for 11 on all three. Dumbbell shrug 80 for 18 on four sets (80 is the top pair, so reps are the only way up). Lying plate neck extension, first time: 10 lb plate, face down on a flat bench with your head off the end and a towel under the plate, 15 reps on both sets; stop and write a note if anything is sharp or sore the next day. Incline curl 30 for 10, 10, logged as you go. Reverse curl 37.5 for 11, 11. Face pulls 32.5 for 15, 15. At build loads (the lighter week runs lighter than these), the next Push B is: shoulder press 50 for 11, chest press 172.5 for 8, lateral raise 17.5 for 14, 14, 14, 13, crossover 32.5 for 12, 12, reverse pec deck 97.5 for 14. Your cable numbers of 30.5 and 50.5 are estimates; the stack gives 30, 32.5 and 50, so use the nearest and log what you set. Dates: build ends 24 November, lighter week 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show on 1 March, 97 days away. Two things I need from you: a morning bodyweight, none logged since 23 August (207 lb), 93 days, and prep starts in 15 days (Bodyweight button on the workout screen); and calves, which get 9 counted sets a week near the bottom of their range and are scored on stage: do you want a second calf lift (smith machine or single-leg dumbbell raise off a step)? Side-delt and calf decisions are dated 1 and 2 December.

flags.note: Push B was logged on 23 November (the first night since 17 November). Pull B is next, tonight 24 November, the last build day.
The lighter week starts 25 November by the calendar whether or not the build week was finished.
Program version 16 changes two rep ranges (shoulder press and chest-supported row, 8 to 12) because the dumbbell rack has no 55 or 65. No sets or lifts changed.
Neck work (lying plate neck flexion on Push A, lying plate neck extension on Pull B tonight, two sets each) has still not been logged. Pull B is 22 sets, Push A 19.
The fourth lateral set was skipped on 23 November (three of four done). If the shrug's fourth set is missing on tonight's Pull B, that card drops to three sets.
More calf work at your gym means a second calf lift (smith machine or single-leg dumbbell calf raise); that is your decision. Until you say, calves stay at three sets a day.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb), 93 days ago; prep starts 9 December and needs a starting number.
The cable weights logged on Push B (30.5 on the crossover, 50.5 on the pushdown) are estimates of 30 and 50: next Push B uses 32.5 and 50, the nearest settings the stack gives.

block.why: Push B on 23 November was the first night logged since Legs A on 17 November, so the six days in between were rest or late logs. Result: every lift on it held or climbed (shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four, chest press 165 for 10 on all three, reverse pec deck 13s), except three misses against the card: the fourth lateral set was skipped, the last rope pushdown set was 11 against 12, and the first overhead extension set was 10 against 12. The build block is doing its job at this gym: every lift logged since 9 November went up or held its weight. Today, 24 November, is the last day of the build block (week 4 of 4, restarted at New York on 28 October). The lighter week is 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, and the show is 97 days away. Program version 16 changes two rep ranges and no sets, no lifts: the shoulder press and the chest-supported row go from 8 to 10 up to 8 to 12 because the dumbbell rack has no 55 or 65 (the previous reviews promised both), so 50 and 60 now have to be built in reps first. The side-delt and calf decisions stay dated (1 and 2 December). If the lighter week does not get trained as planned, the calendar still moves on; that is its call, not mine to move. Executed against plan over the last four weeks the block under-delivered on volume (chest 10.3 of 18 planned, quads 8.3 of 15, lats 10.8 of 18, side delts 6.3 of 10, calves 4.9 of 9, neck 0 of 4); part of that is rest days and partial weeks, part is sets not done, and the two cannot be separated from the weekly totals alone. Prescribed sets rose from 119 to 123 in the block (the four neck sets, never logged). Into assessment: shoulder press 50, chest press 165, row 60, shrug 80, lateral raise 17.5 are the loads to beat.

Push B on 23 November: chest press 165 for 10, 10, 10, the top of Push B's 8 to 10 on every set, up from 165 for 9 on 12 November, and high-to-low crossover 30.5 for 15, 15. Push A lifts repeat from 15 November: chest press 157.5 for 12, 12, 12, smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8, low-to-high crossover 12.5 for 15 on all three. All going up at this gym. Sets hold; the weights move. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 18 are direct sets; 10.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

front-delts.why: Fifteen counted, inside 6 to 16. Eight are the two presses that lead each push day (smith incline 4, shoulder press 4); seven are half credit from the chest press, crossovers and dips. No set is in the week only for front delts, so the only way to lower this is to cut chest or shoulder pressing, and neither should be cut. Shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four sets on 23 November, the first time the top of the range was hit on every set; smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8 on 15 November. Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 15 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 9.1 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

side-delts.why: Raised on 18 November (version 14). Side delts decide how wide the shoulders look on stage; they had the smallest share of any scored muscle (6 direct sets, 8 counted, against 15.5 for rear delts), so lateral raises went to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted with half credit from the shoulder press, the bottom of the 10 to 20 range. First four-set night, 23 November on Push B: 17.5 for 13, 13, 13 and the fourth set was not done, and you asked why four sets for a small muscle. That is answered under your notes. The honest count: the 6.3 a week done is an average over weeks that include rest days and a partial week (the week of 17 to 22 November had no push night) and mostly predate the four-set cards, so it does not prove the fourth set is the problem; there has been exactly one four-set night and three of four sets were done. Direct sets are now 8 against the rear delts' 7; on the counted number it is 10 against 12.5. 15 November on Push A was 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 (three sets, before the fourth existed). The weight is right (17.5, up from 15). The decision between a third lateral day and a second side-delt lift stays with the review of 1 December: the lighter week (25 November to 1 December) cuts sets and is a poor week to add a day, and adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard. By 1 December there will be one more Push A and the lighter-week sessions to read the fourth set by. On the counted number rear delts are at 12.5, still ahead of side delts at 10. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 10 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 6.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

Face pulls stay at two sets on both pull days. Hold. neck.why: Raised on 19 November (version 15) from nothing. You wrote on 18 November that the program had no neck work and that this is an obvious miss in bodybuilding training; you were right, and neck was not even one of the muscles the reviews counted. Neck got, on 19 November, a range of 4 to 12 counted sets a week and two lifts that need only a flat bench and a plate, since you have no harness and no neck machine: lying plate neck flexion, two sets last on Push A (not yet done), and lying plate neck extension, two sets straight after the shrugs on Pull B (not yet done). That is 4 direct sets a week, the bottom of the range, because no neck training appears anywhere in the log and a neck is brought up light and for reps. Both start with a 10 lb plate for 15 to 20 reps. Once both lifts have run twice with all reps done and no neck pain, the next step is a second set day for each, toward 8 a week. Nothing has been done yet, so the four-week average is 0. Held for now: no neck night is logged yet, so the next step waits for two clean runs of each lift.

prep.plan: About two weeks come before prep (15 days from 24 November). Today, 24 November, is the last build day. The week of 25 November is the lighter week: the calendar sets it at about 60 percent of the usual sets with weights about 20 percent lighter, and nothing taken near failure. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (1 December review) and your answer on calves; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 21 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (22 February to 1 March): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the 15 days before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters this week and not in December.

answers.note: Why four sets for a small muscle gorup
answers.answer: Because the side delt is what widens your shoulders on stage, and it was under-worked next to the muscles around it: before 18 November it had 6 direct sets a week. "Small" is about size, not about how much work a muscle can use. The research on weekly hard sets per muscle (Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017) found that 10 or more direct sets a week beat fewer for trained lifters; it is the basis for treating roughly 10 to 20 as the working range, and the ceiling of 20 is my own reading, not the paper's. Four sets on each push day is 8 direct sets a week, which is under 10; it reaches 10 only when the half credit from the shoulder press is added. So four sets is the low end of what the research supports, not an excess. The honest part: on 23 November you did three of the four sets, and this was the first four-set night, so I cannot yet tell whether the fourth set is a problem for you. If it is (tired out by then, short on time, shoulders sore), write it in a note and I will weigh it; your question is not a limit on the number and I did not cut it. Next Push B at build loads: 17.5 for 14, 14, 14, then 13.

Your rack has no 55: it goes 5 lb at a time to 50, then 60, 70, 80 (your 23 July photos), so the next dumbbell is 60, a 10 lb jump that would drop you to about 6 or 7 reps. With the range at 12, the next Push B asks for 50 for 11, then 12, and 60 comes after four 12s. The 19 November review was wrong to say 55.

The first four-set night (23 November) had only three sets done, and your note asks whether four is right for a small muscle. The next step (a third lateral day or a second side-delt lift) is decided at the 1 December review, after the lighter week, by which point one more Push A and the lighter-week sessions are logged. Adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard and land in a week that runs fewer sets; waiting is right because the block needs the fourth set logged before more is piled on it.

Calves sit at 9 counted sets and 6 direct, near the bottom of their range, and they are scored on stage. Your gym has no calf machine (your 23 July photos), so adding calf work means a second calf lift (a standing calf raise on the smith machine, or a single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step), which would take a leg day past the three calf sets you settled in July and August. That is your decision, not mine: it waits for your answer. The 2 December review, at assessment week, is the last point to add it before prep starts on 9 December; if you have not answered by then, calves stay at three sets a day and the review says so.
